result:
The rain started around three in the afternoon, which is the only time I can recall with any clarity the exact moment a Tuesday became weather rather than the opposite. The drops didn't announce themselves so much as arrive — one, then a handful, then the glass filling with a kind of static.

I sat at the kitchen table with a mug that had been lukewarm for twenty minutes, and I did not want to be anywhere else. This is the thing about ordinary weather: it gives you permission to stop. You don't have to be productive, or poetic, or even particularly present. You can just watch a window do its small, repetitive labor of catching and releasing.

There's a particular grief in realizing how few days of your life you'll remember as *the* day. Not bad, not good — just a Tuesday where the light went gold about two seconds before the clouds rolled in and you stood in the doorway of your own kitchen feeling, for no reason you could name, that you were exactly where you were supposed to be.

The rain didn't stop. The mug cooled further. I went back to reading, but I kept looking up. I don't know if that counts as living in the moment, or just being unable to look away from something ordinary because it was doing something quietly magnificent, all by itself, on a pane of glass.
